# Formulas and G10 market notes for sizing

## Formulas (all rates in bp, DV01 in ccy/bp, positive = long duration)

**Risk and VaR**
- Two key rates: `sigma_P = sqrt(KR1^2 s1^2 + KR2^2 s2^2 + 2 KR1 KR2 rho s1 s2)`; N rates: `sqrt(S' Sigma S)` (Tuckman & Serrat, Fixed Income Securities, 4th ed., 2022).
- One factor: vol = DV01 x rate vol (10,000 DV01 x 100bp/yr = $1mm/yr).
- Zero-mean normal: VaR_5% = 1.645 c, VaR_1% = 2.326 c; ES_2.5% = 2.338 c, so for linear rates books VaR_1% ~ ES_2.5% (Darbyshire, Pricing and Trading Interest Rate Derivatives, 2022). Fat tails raise ES without moving VaR.
- Multi-position VaR: `sqrt(sum VaR_i^2 + 2 sum_{i<j} rho_ij VaR_i VaR_j)`. sqrt(k) horizon scaling is valid only for zero-drift iid (IGARCH-type) returns; with drift the k-period quantile is `k mu + z sqrt(k) sigma` (Tsay, Analysis of Financial Time Series, 2010). Non-linear books: resimulate (Golub & Tilman, Risk Management: Approaches for Fixed Income Markets, 2000).
- Horizon should match the time to liquidate: daily for levered or margined books, a month or more for institutional (Golub & Tilman).
- RiskMetrics: `sigma_t^2 = lambda sigma_{t-1}^2 + (1 - lambda) r_{t-1}^2`, lambda 0.94 (half-life 11 days); GARCH(1,1) with omega = 0 and beta = 1 - alpha is exactly EWMA. Short half-lives shrink the effective sample (8-day half-life ~ 23 observations); use fast vols with slow correlations (two-stage). Do not demean (Golub (ed.), BlackRock's Guide to Fixed-Income Risk Management, 2023; Palomar, Portfolio Optimization, 2025).
- Vol-forecast loss for choosing the estimator behind a target: QLIKE = mean(r^2/s2 - log(r^2/s2) - 1) (penalises under-forecasts), MSE on r^2; a high R^2 does not validate a risk model (Paleologo, The Elements of Quantitative Investing, 2025).
- Risk-model check: about 5% of days beyond 2 sd under normal (4.6% two-sided); structural forecasts gave 3% two-sigma exceedances and trailing 3y historical 17% in a 29-fund study (Grinold & Kahn, Active Portfolio Management, 1999).
- Correlation add-on: compare c with the zero-correlation value `sqrt(sum S_i^2 q_ii)`; example 126,091 versus 123,434, residual 2,657 chargeable as an add-on (Darbyshire 2022).
- Event-weighted horizon: weekly sd = `sqrt(sum a_d^2 sigma_d^2)` with weight a_d = 2 for a day twice as volatile.

**Risk allocation**
- Euler: `MRC_i = (Sigma w)_i / sqrt(w'Sigma w)`, `RC_i = w_i MRC_i`, `RRC_i = RC_i / sigma_p` sums to 1. Bucket contribution to CoVaR: `S_i (Q S)_i / c`. PCA form: `(S~_i)^2 lambda_i / c` with `S~ = E'S`, unaffected by eigenvector sign.
- Risk budget b_i: `w_i (Sigma w)_i = b_i w' Sigma w`. Naive solution `w_i ~ sqrt(b_i)/sigma_i`. Risk parity b_i = 1/N lies between minimum variance and equal weight; with extra constraints minimise `sum (RRC_i - b_i)^2`.
- Two assets with Sharpes s1, s2 and correlation rho: optimal vol allocation `v1 ~ (s1 - rho s2)/(1 - rho^2)`; asset 2 is held short if s2/s1 < rho (it hedges).
- HRP: distance `sqrt((1 - rho)/2)`, single linkage, quasi-diagonalise, recursive bisection with `alpha = 1 - V1/(V1 + V2)` (Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning, 2018). Covariance estimation needs at least N(N+1)/2 iid observations for stable inversion.
- Diversification: equal-weight N positions with common correlation rho, `sigma_P = sigma sqrt((1 + (N-1) rho)/N)` -> `sigma sqrt(rho)`. Correlated sources count as one bet: combined IC `IC sqrt(2/(1 + gamma))`.
- Duration bets versus tracking error: IntRR/duration is roughly constant across benchmarks, so limit in duration-years or TE, not as % of benchmark duration (Golub & Tilman 2000). Active risk depends on active position size, not benchmark weight.

**PCA-aware limits**
- Invariant delta-plus-gamma metric (Musaelian, Nagarajan, Villani, PCA: invariant risk metrics, SSRN 2777026, 2016): `dPi = J'a + 0.5 a'H a`, a_i iid N(0,1) (PCs scaled to unit variance), `E[dPi^2] = ||J||^2 + 0.5 ||H||_F^2 + 0.25 (Tr H)^2`; sensitivities by central differences. One rotation-invariant limit caps linear and convexity risk and aggregates across currencies without aligning PC signs.
- Tail extension (mixed normal: all PCs jump together with probability p and scale theta): `(1 + p(theta^2 - 1)) ||J||^2 + (1 + p(theta^4 - 1))(0.5 ||H||_F^2 + 0.25 (Tr H)^2)`. p = 10%, theta = 5 doubles risk for swaps and multiplies it ~8x for straddles. Empirical PC excess kurtosis (1y): 1.2, 6.4, 8.8, 18.3, 30.2 for PC1-5. After calm periods PC vols drift down and the metric flatters; use the tail version.
- Flylets: (n-2) unit-norm three-adjacent-node vectors orthogonal to PC1 and PC2; PC1/PC2-neutral 2y5y7y and 5y10y15y flies look negligible in the invariant metric but carry large flylet exposure. Keep PC and flylet limits separate; gross-notional limits are crude.
- Minimum-VaR fly (belly fixed at 2): `w_wings = -Q_ww^-1 Q_wb s`, e.g. (-1.48, 2.00, -0.38) for EUR 2/5/10; minimal-change PC1-neutral weights solve `min d'd` s.t. `(x + d)'p = 0`, giving (-1.10, 2, -1.08) from (-1, 2, -1) (Quantitative Finance Stack Exchange, "How to adjust butterfly 2s5s10s swaps trade for directionality?", 2018-21). Out of sample, regression weights had the smallest vol, min-VaR almost the same.
- Factor shares of $100k-DV01 packages (level / slope / curvature, user's own research): 5Y/30Y 5.1 / 88.9 / 6.0%; 30Y/50Y 43.3 / 29.3 / 27.4%; 20Yx5Y/25Yx5Y 69.0 / 14.7 / 16.4%; 10Yx10Y/20Yx10Y 61.3 / 0.2 / 38.5%. Slope-to-convexity ratio spans 130x across structures, so say which factor the sizing rule exposes before quoting P&L. PC1-neutral tight pairs cut level risk 88 / 66 / 96% and kept 88 / 89 / 67% of net P&L; PC1+PC2-neutral on 5Y/30Y lost 739.8bp as its P&L had been the slope bet. Costs: break-even 1.21 / 1.63 / 1.35bp per leg versus 0.25bp charged; report P&L at 0x / 0.5x / 1x / 2x costs.
- Practitioner view: PCA was of limited use for day-to-day risk management in one swaps text and CoVaR performed better (Darbyshire 2022); use PCA for hedge construction and explanation, CoVaR for the limit.

**Second-order and carry-adjusted selection**
- IRS gamma (parallel moves): `G = -(2S/10,000) sum_{j=h..i} j a_j` with discount-factor-weighted `a_j` (h, i = first and last payment year); with unit discount factors `G ~ -(h + i) S/10,000` PV01 per bp; 5Y5Y (h = 6, i = 10) with $50,000 PV01 -> ~-$80 of PV01 per bp (DF-weighted -79.8). Rank spread trades by second-order ex-ante Sharpe (annual roll-down over P&L vol including 0.5 G sigma^2 and correlation), not first-order roll / vol. Roll-down strategies are short vol and crowded.
- Ex-ante Sharpe for ranking mixed packages: implied 3m carry and roll / 3m realised vol (annualised). Carry/R = Sharpe / (1 + |R|), R = correlation to outright rates, penalises disguised duration (Goldman Sachs, Global Rates Best Trade Report, 30 Sep 2026). Carry-to-vol sizing: if you rank on carry/vol you must size by vol, otherwise the carry of low-vol legs is not earned (simple carry 0.74, vol-sized 0.71, ranked on carry/vol but equal sized 0.66, ranked and sized by vol 0.89; Willer & Saunders, 2026).
- Optimal OU leverage (Jurek and Yang, log utility): `N_t = ((lambda (Pbar - P_t) - r P_t)/sigma^2) W_t`; steady state leverage is normal; with zero mean and fund flows f, leverage stays below `M = alpha (lambda + r)/((1 + f) sigma sqrt(2 lambda))` with confidence N(alpha) (d'Aspremont, Identifying Small Mean Reverting Portfolios, 2008). Most mean reversion is captured with 3-5 legs.

**Conviction functions** (Lopez de Prado 2018)
- Probability to size: `z = (p - 0.5)/sqrt(p(1-p))`, `m = 2 Phi(z) - 1`; multi-class `z = (p~ - 1/||X||)/sqrt(p~(1 - p~))`.
- Average active bets: size at t = mean of sizes of bets with start <= t < end. Discretise `m* = round(m/d) d`.
- Sigmoid in divergence x (forecast - price): `m = x/sqrt(w + x^2)`, target `q = int[m Q]`, calibrate `w = x^2 (m*^-2 - 1)`; limit price = average of inverse sizes between current and target position (e.g. m* = 0.95 at x = 10, Q = 100 -> q = 97).
- Concurrency: c_t = longs - shorts; budget `m = c_l/max c_l - c_s/max c_s`.
- Meta-labelling: the primary model sets side, a secondary model's probability sizes the bet; high accuracy on small bets with low accuracy on large bets ruins the book.
- Qualitative views to scores (Grinold & Kahn Table 19.3): very positive +1.73, positive +0.87, none 0, negative -0.87, very negative -1.73; IC 0.1 ~ right 55% of the time.
- Signal as fraction of risk limit: a systematic score of -0.2 means short 20% of the risk limit. Example duration weights: PMI 15%, revisions 15%, bond momentum 20%, equity momentum 15%, carry-to-risk 35% (J.P. Morgan, Update on systematic rule based trading strategies, 2017-18).

**Cost and turnover**
- Round trip: `r_net = r_gross - 2c`; annualised `r_net = r_gross - 2c/n` for an n-year hold. Square-root impact: impact (bp) = alpha sqrt(size), average cost (2 alpha/3) sqrt(size), alpha = 1/1000 -> 1mm risk costs 1bp. Inventory-aware add-on for building size in pieces: `(2/3) alpha (|x + x_inv|^1.5 - |x_inv|^1.5)`, floored at zero for risk-reducing trades. Example (cost per PV01 = 0.5bp half-spread + impact): 100,000 PV01 in 10Y costs 0.71bp on average (50,000 + 21,081 add-on); building it as two 50,000 clips costs 0.65bp (25,000 + 7,453) then 0.77bp (25,000 + 13,628), averaging to the same 0.71bp (Darbyshire 2022).
- >= 75% of incremental value added comes with 50% of turnover; optimal turnover where the frontier slope equals round-trip cost (Grinold & Kahn). No-trade band widens with proportional cost (Constantinides). Rule of thumb order <= 1% of ADV (Chan 2009; from equities, treat as an upper bound in rates).

## G10 market notes for sizing
Relative vol statistics are from 2000-2018 swap returns (Macrosynergy, Interest rate swap returns: empirical lessons) and move with regime; recompute from `curve_par`.

| Ccy | Vol / correlation facts | Sizing consequence |
|---|---|---|
| USD | highest developed-market IRS vol (~3.5% annualised in that sample); 10y swap vol 7.3bp/day in the 45 days around regime breaks versus 5.2bp outside (Tuckman, Lehman LMR, Oct 2003); repo mostly bilateral-uncleared with near-zero haircuts in RV (Conks, Demystifying the Repo Market Part III, 28 May 2024); 3m STIR contract = $25 per bp per contract | size by DV01 and by cash/margin; basis and swap-spread trades are balance-sheet bound; payrolls-day vol ~2x normal |
| EUR | EGB repo via CCPs whose haircuts can change unilaterally (3% -> 80% for IE/PT, July 2011); small deliverable baskets, fixed delivery day; EUR-GBP / CHF / SEK monthly return correlation ~0.8; 2Y3Y-5Y5Y correlation 0.87, 10Y20Y-30Y20Y 0.96 | haircut-stress sizing for periphery spreads; BPV-match STIR vs bond futures (10 two-year bond futures per bundle in the source example); treat the 0.87-0.96 forward-grid correlations as "one bet" |
| GBP | large-block leakage (200mm 10y IRS versus typical 25-50mm moved mid ~2bp, spread 1.25 -> 1.75bp); ERM exit 1992 (rates 10% -> 12%, threat of 15%) as the "deep play" case; gilt futures CTD can drop out on ex-dividend rules | cap clip size to ~2x typical; stand aside in disorderly regimes; correlation of STIR packs regime-dependent |
| JPY | lowest vol (~1%; relative sd versus USD ~0.3) and lowest correlation (0.2-0.3) with other developed markets; official-sector buying has cut JGB liquidity to a trickle; mechanical carry breaks under yield-curve control | vol-matched cross-market legs need roughly 3x the DV01 of the USD leg (derived from relative sd 0.3, FX-hedged); the vol estimate must cover the policy regime; liquidity-limited sizing |
| CHF | lowest monthly IRS sd (~45bp), relative sd versus USD ~0.5; risk-off low-yielder rally; vol targeting produced larger outliers | DV01 about 2x per unit of USD vol; do not rely on vol-targeted sizing; risk-off correlation with funding currencies |
| CAD | correlation with USD ~0.8, relative sd ~0.8-0.9; swaps against US futures margin offset ~50% | little diversification against USD books; offsets only with a clearer that accepts the pair |
| AUD / NZD | AUD-NZD monthly return correlation ~0.8; AUD futures-versus-swap margin offset ~50%; AUD 1y2s5s10s fly with +/-100k DV01 legs had a 5-year 5-day 95% HVaR of 801k (Citi Trade Ideas Radar, 13 Aug 2026) | treat AUD + NZD as one risk block for the currency cap; systematic signals expressed as fractions of the risk limit (AU +0.8, NZ -0.2 in the J.P. Morgan example) |
| SEK / NOK | NOK-SEK correlation ~0.7; NOK benchmark IRS has few contributors, wide markets, sometimes no trading; SEK 5y IRS 50mm best aggregated quote ~0.75bp wide (Darbyshire 2022) | smaller clips, wider stops, valuation-uncertainty haircut on the stop budget |

Other notes: UST top-of-book width about 0.4bp in 2s, 0.2-0.3bp in 5s and 10s, 0.1-0.2bp in 30s (J.P. Morgan, TradeRunner, 16 Aug 2018): use as a floor on cost per leg for small clips. DM trades in the Citi radar need >= 100k DV01 (EM >= 40k) to count as executable: below this a package is "paper" in size terms. Cross-market betas estimated on daily data understate correlation because of time zones: blend with weekly. Hedge parameters should be fixed a priori (anti-overfitting).
Policy-meeting basis: hedge contracts whose averaging window spans a policy meeting carry meeting-date basis risk; stack into the prior contract if most variance is policy.
